results.change_intent: Skip regenerating fourslash tests that have been designated as manual tests.
results.summary: The change introduces an unhandled exception if manualTests.txt does not exist and uses a key format that does not match the test names written by makeManual.mts.

issues.comment: If manualTests.txt does not exist yet (e.g., on a clean clone before any manual tests are created), fs.readFileSync will throw an unhandled ENOENT error and crash the script.
issues.suggestion: Check if manualTestsPath exists before attempting to read it, returning an empty set if it is absent.

issues.comment: makeManual.mts populates manualTests.txt using the filename in genDir (e.g., foo_test.go), but this check looks up the capitalized base name testName (e.g., Foo). Because of this format mismatch, manualTests.has(testName) will evaluate to false and the test will not be skipped.
issues.suggestion: Ensure the format checked here matches what makeManual.mts writes to manualTests.txt, such as checking `${test.name}_test.go` or test.name.

results.change_intent: Add a script to move a generated fourslash test to the manual tests directory and record it in manualTests.txt so it won't be overwritten.
results.summary: The script does not format test names consistently with convertFourslash.mts, causing file resolution failures and preventing manual tests from actually being skipped during regeneration.

issues.comment: There is a mismatch in how test files are named on disk and how test names are recorded for skipping in convertFourslash.mts. In convertFourslash.mts, generated files are named `${test.name}_test.go`, and tests are skipped if manualTests contains `test.name[0].toUpperCase() + test.name.substring(1)`. In this script, if the user passes `foo` (as shown in the PR description `npm run manualtest testname`), `genTestFile` checks for `genDir/foo` instead of `foo_test.go` and exits with an error. If the user passes `foo_test.go`, `foo_test.go` is written to `manualTests.txt`, but convertFourslash.mts will check for `Foo` (capitalized and without `_test.go`), causing convertFourslash to regenerate the file anyway.
issues.suggestion: Normalize the input argument: resolve the file on disk by appending `_test.go` if omitted, and format the name written to `manualTests.txt` to match the capitalized test name format checked by convertFourslash (e.g. strip `_test.go` and capitalize the first letter).

issues.comment: When no arguments are supplied, the script exits without printing usage instructions or an error message.
issues.suggestion: Log a usage message to `console.error` before exiting.

results.change_intent: Add a `makemanual` npm script to run `internal/fourslash/_scripts/makeManual.mts`.
results.summary: The new npm script correctly references the new TypeScript script and matches existing conventions in the file.
